description: AUTHORITATIVE Aforo usage-ingestor ingest contract. Derived from the REAL controllers + request DTOs in aforo-nextgen-usage-ingestor-service — never from any SDK's own constants. Every SDK test suite in this repo loads THIS file and asserts its observed wire request (endpoint path + body shape) against it. Guard purpose (A+ delivery-guarantee prompt 7): the 2026-07-05 D1 incident shipped 16 transport-variant SDKs that posted a BATCH body to /v1/ingest/events (a SINGLE-event endpoint) — every real flush 400'd, 100% event loss, hidden by 17 green suites that each asserted the SDK's OWN wrong constant. A test that validates the SDK against the SDK has zero contract coverage; this file is the independent source of truth.
maintenance: If an ingest endpoint or request DTO changes in aforo-nextgen-usage-ingestor-service, update this file FROM THE CONTROLLER/DTO CODE (re-verify the file:line references below) in the same change that updates the SDKs. Never edit this file to match an SDK — that inverts the guard.

/v1/ingest.notes: Binds ONE event. Posting a batch wrapper {events:[...]} here 400s (customerId/metricName/... missing at top level). Per-event customerId is required — there is no header/tenant fallback on this DTO.

/v1/ingest/events.notes: Apigee-format SINGLE event (this was the D1 bug: transport variants posted {events:[...]} here and every flush 400'd). customerId is @NotBlank @Size(max=64) since usage-ingestor f37c1db (re-verified 2026-10-01) — the old tenant fallback billed usage to a customer that was really the tenant. idempotencyKey is @NotBlank since 2026-07-05.

/v1/ingest/batch.notes: Body is an OBJECT {"events":[...]}, not a bare array (bare array = /v1/ingest/async-batch shape). Each element is a full IngestUsageEventRequest incl. per-event customerId + idempotencyKey. The gql*/grpc*/ws*/mqtt* protocol fields the transport variants send live on this event DTO (V14) and are optional.

/v1/ingest/async-batch.notes: Body is a BARE JSON ARRAY of events (no {events:} wrapper). No SDK in this repo targets it today; documented so the array-vs-wrapper distinction can't be guessed wrong.

/api/v1/ingest/compound.notes: correlationId is UUID-TYPED server-side — a non-UUID string 400s and silently drops the event (Rule #21 / 2026-07-05 gateway freeze). ONLY the /api-prefixed path exists; /v1/ingest/compound is NOT mapped. Used by gateway plugins, not by SDKs in this repo.

/api/v1/ingest/compound/batch.notes: Batch of compound events. Same UUID correlationId constraint per element. No SDK in this repo targets it today.

responses.description: Shape of 2xx RESPONSE bodies. aforo-common's ApiResponseAdvice wraps every 2xx JSON controller body in {success, data, meta} (only /internal/, /actuator and the API-doc paths are excluded), so the DTO a controller returns arrives under 'data'. A client that reads a DTO field at the top level sees undefined and silently does nothing — this is how mcp-proxy quota enforcement never denied, and how no SDK counted per-event rejections or saw killedSessionIds (all fixed 2026-10-01). Every client in this repo reads 'data' when it is an object and falls back to the bare body. Error bodies (4xx/5xx, RFC 7807 ProblemDetail) are NOT wrapped.

derivedFrom.quotaCheck: aforo-nextgen-usage-ingestor-service preflight/PreFlightQuotaController.java (POST /api/v1/quota/check, always 200) + dto/PreFlightCheckRequest.java (customerId @NotBlank; metricName, estimatedQuantity optional) + dto/PreFlightCheckResponse.java (@JsonInclude NON_NULL)

/api/v1/quota/check.notes: Always HTTP 200 — the decision is in the body. The server fails open (ALLOW) on its own errors; clients fail open on timeout, non-200, or a body with no recognisable decision.

schemas.$comment: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the request bodies the SDKs send. maxLength = the ingestor's @Size(max) and counts UTF-16 code units (Java String.length()), not code points. Unknown properties are ignored by the server (@JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true)). contract/verify-ingestor.mjs checks every maxLength and required field against the DTO source.

transportPolicy.$comment: Normative behaviour of every SDK's transport core (contract/TRANSPORT-SPEC.md explains each rule). Each SDK's contract test reads these numbers; a change here goes in before the SDK change.

headers.notes: The API key goes in X-API-Key only — never in the URL, the body, logs, repr/toString or error messages.

batch.notes: A flush sends at most defaultEvents (configurable up to maxEvents) per request and splits a batch whose JSON body would exceed targetRequestBodyBytes. 413 splits the batch in half; a single event that still gets 413 is dropped as rejected.

queue.notes: One bounded queue and ONE long-lived flusher per client. track() never starts a thread/goroutine/task or sends; it enqueues and, at the flush threshold, wakes the flusher. Overflow evicts the oldest event and reports it through onDrop('overflow').

timeouts.notes: requestMs is a TOTAL deadline for the whole exchange, including reading the response body. close/shutdown is bounded by shutdownMs: the flusher keeps retrying until the deadline, each request uses min(requestMs, time left), and events still queued or in flight at the deadline are reported through onDrop('shutdown').

retry.formula: delay = random(0, min(maxDelayMs, baseMs * 2^attempt)); with Retry-After: max(retryAfter, that delay), capped at retryAfter.maxMs
retry.dropOnStatus: any other 4xx (400, 404, 405, 409, 415, 422): the batch is rejected — onDrop('rejected'), never retried
retry.perEventRetryable: 2xx with errors[].retryable=true: those events go back to the queue (keys kept) and are re-sent after the jittered backoff, at most maxRetries times, then treated as an outage; retryable=false events are dropped as 'rejected'. errors[] is authoritative even when 'failed' is missing or 0.
retry.redirects: never followed; a 3xx is an outage like 401/403 (requeue + breaker, ERROR log naming the target host) so the API key never reaches another host

afterRetriesExhausted.notes: A batch that still fails after maxRetries (network error, timeout, retryable status, 401/403) goes back to the FRONT of the queue with the same idempotency keys, and the flusher pauses for the breaker cooldown. Events keep arriving into the bounded queue; overflow is reported as 'overflow'. 401/403 log an ERROR naming the status (bad or revoked API key) once per breaker opening. The next successful send closes the breaker. Re-sends are dedup-safe because the ingestor deduplicates on idempotencyKey.

transportPolicy.dropReasonNotes: retry_exhausted is kept for API compatibility; with requeue-and-open-breaker it is only reported when the client is closed and requeue is impossible. 'closed' = track() after close (no exception). 'shutdown' = still queued when the shutdown deadline passed.

compression.reason: usage-ingestor decodes Content-Encoding: gzip on the JSON ingest endpoints (GzipRequestFilter, wave 8, G269), with the decoded body capped at maxRequestBodyBytes (413 past it). SDKs gzip batch bodies of minBytes or more; smaller bodies go plain. Any other coding is answered 415 with Accept-Encoding: gzip. Every SDK has an option to turn compression off (compression = none).

identity.notes: Decision (Jay, 2026-10-26): every integration that meters an incoming request (HTTP middleware, gRPC/GraphQL/WS/MQTT interceptors, MCP servers, servlet filters) needs a customer resolver the caller supplies from authenticated identity. Reading a caller-controlled value (X-Customer-Id header, gRPC metadata, MCP _meta.customer_id, MQTT username) needs an explicit opt-in named trustCustomerHeader / trust_customer_header / TrustCustomerHeader (per language). With neither, construction fails with a configuration error. There is no fallback to 'unknown', 'anonymous' or the agent id. A resolver that returns nothing for a request: the event is dropped with reason 'invalid' and counted.

transportPolicy.connections: One pooled HTTP client per SDK client, reused for every request; closed on close().
